content: Zinc gluconate is a lozenge that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of the common cold. It is specifically designed to reduce the severity and duration of cold symptoms, including cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, sneezing, post-nasal drip, and hoarseness. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, it is recommended to begin treatment as soon as symptoms appear, ideally within 24 to 48 hours of onset. The lozenge should be completely dissolved in the mouth and not chewed. The recommended daily dosage is six lozenges for adults and four lozenges for individuals aged 12 to 17. Children under the age of 12 should consult a healthcare professional before use. The lozenges should be taken every 2 to 4 hours as needed until symptoms subside. Zinc gluconate may interact with certain medications, such as minocycline, doxycycline, tetracycline, or coumadin (warfarin). Zinc can inhibit the absorption of these drugs, so it is important to consult a healthcare provider before use if you are taking any of these medications. If symptoms persist beyond seven days, it is advised to stop use and consult a healthcare professional. It is also important to note that this product is not intended to treat influenza or allergies. Patients with diabetes should be aware that sugar replacements in the product may affect blood sugar levels. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare provider before using this product. The lozenges should be kept out of reach of children. To avoid minor stomach upset, it is recommended not to take the lozenges on an empty stomach. Additionally, citrus fruits, juices, or products containing citric acid should be avoided for at least 30 minutes before and after taking the lozenges, as they may reduce the product's effectiveness. It is advised to drink plenty of fluids during treatment. The product should be stored in a cool, dry place after opening. Zinc gluconate is gluten-free but may produce a laxative effect in some individuals. The interaction between alcohol and zinc gluconate has not been established, so patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol consumption while using this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name Cold-EEZE® and is available in various flavors, including wild cherry. It is clinically proven to reduce the duration of the common cold and is recommended by pharmacists.
